correctness.rationale: The exact symmetric system gives determinant factor D=1−(1+2z+2z²)e^(−2z)>0 at z=ta>0; the antisymmetric eigenvalue 1−j is positive too. The outer numerator has a pointwise positive integrand: after ordering u≤v and removing e^(−u−v), its slope in v is e^(2u)−1−2u>0, and it is positive at v=u. In the center factorization put p=e^(−z). The t-scaled numerator is 2(1−p)[1−(1+2z)p]+e^(−t)z(1+t−z)(1−p²), which yields the stated F_b for b=(1−a)/a. Its cubic coefficient is 5/6−b², and e^z dominates for large z. For b≤sqrt(5/6), (1+bz)e^(−bz)≥1−5z²/12; the resulting lower bound multiplied by e^z has zero coefficients through degree 3 and positive higher coefficients by A_4=8 and the displayed induction. Thus strict positivity at the boundary holds at every finite t>0, not in the flat limit. Dividing by D~4z³/3 and using the center Gram equation gives the displayed two flat limits with normalization dx/2. No uniqueness of the subcritical t-crossing follows or is claimed.
residual_risks: This is an exact-arithmetic result for three fixed symmetric nodes with neither nugget nor augmentation. It does not settle conditioning or other designs.
